nodes.summary: Let `G` be a Gröbner basis of an ideal `I ⊆ k[x₀, x₁, …]` for the lexicographic order `x₀ > x₁ > ⋯`, and let `S` be a final segment of the variables, such as `{x_l, x_{l+1}, …}`. Then the leading monomial of every nonzero polynomial of the elimination ideal `I ∩ k[S]` is divisible by the leading monomial of an element of `G ∩ k[S]`: the elements of `G` that involve only the variables in `S` form a Gröbner basis of…
nodes.title: Elimination Theorem

nodes.summary: Let `m` be a monomial order and `G` a set of nonzero polynomials over a field. If for all `g, h ∈ G` the S-polynomial `S(g, h)` can be written as `∑_{b ∈ G} q_b b` with no summand of leading monomial above that of `S(g, h)`, then `G` is a Gröbner basis of the ideal it generates.
nodes.title: Buchberger's criterion

nodes.summary: For a monomial order `m`, a set `G` of polynomials is a Gröbner basis of the ideal `I` when `G ⊆ I` and the leading monomial of every nonzero `f ∈ I` is divisible by the leading monomial of some nonzero `g ∈ G` (`m.degree g ≤ m.degree f` componentwise). Equivalently, the leading terms of `G` generate the initial ideal `in_m(I)`. Finite `G` is not required.
nodes.title: Gröbner basis

nodes.summary: If every variable outside `S` comes before every variable in `S`, and the exponent vector `e` vanishes outside `S`, then every `d` that is lexicographically at most `e` vanishes outside `S`.
nodes.title: Lexicographic order and final segments of variables

nodes.summary: Let `G` be a Gröbner basis of an ideal `I` for a monomial order, and write `f = ∑_{b ∈ G} q_b b + r` where no monomial of `r` is divisible by the leading monomial of any `b ∈ G`, as the division algorithm produces. Then `f ∈ I` if and only if `r = 0`.
nodes.title: Ideal membership by remainder zero

nodes.summary: If `G` is a Gröbner basis of `I` and `g, h ∈ G`, then every remainder of `S(g, h)` on division by `G` is zero: the easy direction of Buchberger's criterion, since `S(g, h) ∈ I`.
nodes.title: S-polynomials of a Gröbner basis reduce to zero

nodes.summary: If `G` is a Gröbner basis of `I`, then `I` is the ideal generated by `G`. The proof divides by the nonzero elements of `G`, whose leading coefficients are units, and applies the remainder criterion.
nodes.title: A Gröbner basis generates its ideal

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
